name: look-up
story: Seen in three-quarter view, turned toward us, holding her bump with both hands the way an expectant mother does: one hand curled a little over its top, the other cradling it from beneath. She is looking down at her bump with a tender smile. Then she looks up from her bump to us, the viewer, and smiles warmly, holding our eyes for a moment, before her gaze drifts back down to her bump.
intensity: gentle, warm and intimate: a private moment that turns into a quiet connection with the viewer. Unhurried; the look up is the one clear move, nothing big or fast.
handsBoxNote: film px holding both hands all shot: blind_ab.py and critic_F.py draw them at 1:1 and their motion per second (lesson 58)

keys.note: looking down at her bump (still q_k_down_0), the upper back rounded a little over it
anticipation: a touch deeper into the nod, the shoulders settle
half way up, the eyes already on us (still q_k_mid_2)

head up, eye contact (still q_k_up_1), a long soft arrival; the chest opens and the shoulders rise 4 frames BEHIND the head and settle after it (v1: the head pivoted on a still torso); v6: arrives at 3.35 s (the lift took 0.3 s at 2.1–2.4: brisk next to the 1.7 s return)
a moving hold: the head tips a little (warm tilt)
the head starts down a few frames after the eyes (v1 waited 0.7 s with the eyes down: aloof)
back down on its own softer path: forward and tipped toward the bump, not the look up in reverse
settles back into the look down (1.8 s, a drift with a long soft landing; v2's 7.1 read as a dead stop); the shoulders soften after the head arrives

near.note: the near hand cradles the underside of the bump, palm up, the thumb on its lower front (still q_k4_down_0; Harry's pick 2026-10-13). Pinned to the belly so it rides her breath and the look up; keepSize holds its drawn size. v17 put every stop 0.06 H further forward so the tips reached the bump's front edge as in the still; blind, the tips meeting the edge read as 'an awkward tangent' and the hand 'oversized, like a paw' (v17 lost to v14), so v18 keeps v14's place and instead lays the fingers at the still's ANGLE (n-down's hand.near, refs/derive_lookup.sh): the film had them 6° steeper than the fitted key (tools/finger_angles.mjs; QA 'fingers' gate, lesson 58). v20 puts it where the still does: at 0 s the film's tips sat 26 px behind the still's (the fitted arm on n-down's trunk, whose bump front matches the still's to 2 px: tools/mask_overlay.py), so every stop moves (+0.124, −0.005) H and the tips land on q_k4_down_0's, the index at the bump's edge as the still draws it (natural lens v15, v17, v18: 'the tips stop well inside the edge'; v17's half-way move with the fingers 6° too steep read 'a tangent')

the lower hand strokes up along the underside and back (~6 px), half a beat behind the top hand (overlap, never in unison). On the still's tips (v20) a stroke toward the front pushed the middle tip past the bump's edge at 1.0 s (blind A/B v20; tip_check)
the cradle lifts the bump a touch (~11 px) as she breathes in to look up: she feels its weight
then strokes forward under it as the smile eases

far.note: the far hand curled a little over the TOP of the bump, the fingers together and gently curved over the dome, its arm coming down past her bust and round the bump's side (still q_k4_down_0; Harry on v5's flat hand with its arm hidden: 'still looks creepy and lifeless. Rather than being a little curled over the top of the bump'). Pinned to the belly, so it rides the breath and the look up; drawn over the dress by zBias. keepSize holds its drawn size while her body moves under it. keyedArm: the arm stays the fitted one (the 3D solve wandered its elbow 40 px)

while she looks down the top hand caresses the dome: the wrist slides ~6 px down its front and back while the hand turns about it (fidget hand.far) so the fingertips sweep ~15 px (v6 draft's 3 px moves were invisible at phone size: 'the hands look identical in every frame', natural lens and blind A/B). A wrist SLIDE of 14-18 px instead hid the forearm behind her bust (the strip past its edge lost 35% of its area: the arm 'shrinking', lesson 39)
as she smiles at us, a long slow stroke: the wrist slides ~7 px down the dome while the hand turns about it, the fingertips sweeping ~18 px; the hands answer her smile
and a small one as her eyes come back to the bump

keys.note: the eyes lead the head, a beat ahead, not before it: the lids lift with the gaze as the head starts up (v17's lift at 1.6-2.05 s, while the head still sank into the dip, read as 'peeking up from under her brow', natural lens v17)
the smile reaches the eyes: the lower lids arch up a little
and eases off a little: the hold lives

the eyes go back to the bump a beat ahead of the head, not before it moves (the head leaves n-up at 5.5, n-ret at 6.4): at 5.8 s the forward gaze under a still-raised head read 'a sideways glance… side-eye' (natural lens v14, v18)
the tender smile still closed as the head comes up
the beam blooms as the head lands: she sees us, then smiles
the lips close over 0.55 s, a beat behind the eyes

breath.note: a breath in starts with the eyes' lift (1.8 s) and peaks in the eye contact; gain up from mum3's (v1: the chest moved ≤ 1 px); v6: belly 0.016 → 0.022, chest 0.045 → 0.055 (natural lens: 'no visible breathing')

events.note: a slow, warm blink at us

fidget.note: the near thumb strokes the bump's lower front, out and back (the cradling hand's life is in its thumb, the one digit we see on the bump) (v7: amplitudes ×1.5–1.7; at the old size both fresh reviewers saw the hands "identical in every frame" at phone size, lesson 52) v18: the thumb's swing halved (ts −26 → −13) and the whole hand turning ~4° with it: the full swing alone read 'a thumb tic… a straight stalk' (blind A/Bs v17, v18 vs v14); v19's curl instead was too small to see and lost to this (6 vs 6.5)

as she lifts her eyes to us the cradling fingers gather under the bump ('holding you', bringing the baby with her) and release (v7: starts with the look up, 1.5× larger: 'nothing happens with the hands when she looks up at us')

a second, smaller thumb stroke as the smile eases v18: the thumb's swing halved (ts −26 → −13) and the whole hand turning ~4° with it: the full swing alone read 'a thumb tic… a straight stalk' (blind A/Bs v17, v18 vs v14); v19's curl instead was too small to see and lost to this (6 vs 6.5)
as her gaze comes back the near fingers re-settle, index first

the top hand's fingers breathe while she looks down, after the thumb stroke has begun (overlap, never in unison): the index lifts a touch and the fingers ease apart by a degree or two (they lie together, as in the still) (v7: 2-3× larger, every finger: the top hand's visible life is in its fingers. Its turn about the wrist (hand.far) barely shows: the hand lies palm down on the dome, so a turn in its own plane is seen nearly edge-on; 24° moved the tips ~6 px)

'holding you' on the top hand too, 4–5 frames behind the near one: the fingers press down over the dome (a little more bend at the knuckles, the finger joints straightening) and gather, then release. v9's curl into the finger joints (+12–16° each) bunched the draped hand into 'a paw' (natural lens; lesson 54)
the top hand's index lifts and settles back as the smile eases (a small tap of affection)

as the smile blooms the top hand gives the bump a small squeeze (the fingers press on over the dome, the wrist dips) and lets go: the hands answer her smile (natural lens: 'nothing answers the smile at 3.0–3.4 s'). A draped hand presses at its knuckles: v9's +11–14° into a 48° bend curled it to a block (lesson 54). v17: half again as much (knuckles +7–10°, the finger joints straightening 4°, the wrist dipping 14°): at +4–6° neither blind reviewer saw it at phone size ('neither hand presses, shifts or settles' as she smiles)
and the near thumb presses with it, 3 frames later. v17: the cradling fingers gather with it (+4–6° at the knuckles) and the thumb presses further

the caress: the top hand turns on the dome about its wrist (hand.far, in its own plane) and back, the fingertips sweeping ~25 px. A turn of the forearm (foreRot) swept them as far but twisted the forearm's drawn edges off the underbust, opening a white gap between bust, arm and hand (up to 73 px) (v7: amplitudes ×1.5–1.7; at the old size both fresh reviewers saw the hands "identical in every frame" at phone size, lesson 52). v8: the arm hanging at her side with the forearm end-on, a 24–26° turn grew the drawn hand 12% (qa limbs): 14–17° keeps it within 10%
the stroke as she smiles: the same turn, a little larger
and a small one as her eyes come back to the bump
as her eyes come back to the bump the top hand's fingers lift a little and settle back onto it, index first

a small thumb stroke over the loop's seam (v6: both hands dead still from 7.4 s round to 0.4 s) v18: the thumb's swing halved (ts −26 → −13) and the whole hand turning ~4° with it: the full swing alone read 'a thumb tic… a straight stalk' (blind A/Bs v17, v18 vs v14); v19's curl instead was too small to see and lost to this (6 vs 6.5)
and the top hand eases round on the dome with it, into the loop

hand.far.note: the top hand lies across the dome as the still q_k4_down_0 draws it: its wrist, middle knuckle and each fingertip placed on the still's (hand_place --tips), drawn at 85–90% of its length (palm down onto the dome, --palm-down 0.55, the fingers bent down over it at the knuckles; v8's centroid fit drew it at 73%, the fingers flat and bunched, lesson 54). Its caress turns it about the wrist by 14–17° (hand.far fidgets): at 24–26° the turn grew the hand 12% (v8 draft)

forearm.far.hidden: the far arm hangs at her side (still q_k4_down_0): the upper arm is the strip past her bust, drawn near full length; the forearm points at us over the top of the bump from the elbow on its edge, drawn END-ON as the still's round mass (parts/arms.js, 13–18% of its length: its size is the cross-section's, so it never reads as shrinking; lesson 53)

hand.near.note: the cradling hand lies palm up under the bump, turned a little from us as in the still q_k4_down_0: drawn at 76% of its length all shot (it never changes, so it can't read as shrinking). Fitted to the still's four tips it matches the still's hand best there (tools/mask_overlay.py: 1166 px of mismatch; held near full length with --hand-len 0.85, 91%, it was 1431 px, the little finger hidden and the hand tipped down; lesson 56). v18 laid it at the still's finger angle (n-down's hand.near 35.4, QA 'fingers'): 70–76% of its length (the least at the thumb stroke's 4° turn, 1.0 s), the fingers at the still's lengths (finger_angles 56/54/50/42 px, the key 57/55/51/43), holding its size within 1.03

fingers.note: the cradling hand's fingers as the still q_k4_down_0 lays them (fit-q_k4_down, fitted to its four tips) at the look-down frames: v17's film had them 6° steeper than the key (n-down's trunk turned the hand with it), read as 'straight, parallel, a comb' (natural lens v17; lesson 58)
the top hand's fingers draped over the dome as the still q_k4_down_0 (lesson 54)

preflight.1: both arms placed on still q_k4_down_0 by hand_place --natural (elbows at her sides, the far arm coming down past her bust and round the bump's side), on the look-down key's trunk
preflight.2: every key's hands judged against q_k4_down_0 in ref_match sheets: the far hand curled over the top with the fingers together, the near hand cradling with its thumb on the lower front
preflight.3: qa limbs gate on every frame; the far hand's foreshortening is the still's (qa.limbs note)
preflight.6: both hands hold the bump the whole shot; none hangs
preflight.7: top hand: palm on the dome, fingers together and gently curved over it (hold); lower hand cups from beneath (cradle); no fingers off the outline
preflight.9: both arms visible and joined: the far forearm runs down past the bust into the hand (no hidden-arm hand stuck on, v5)
preflight.10: each hand gets its own small acts at its own times: the near thumb strokes (0.2 s, 4.6 s), the cradle lifts the bump a touch on the breath in (0.8–3 s), the near fingers gather (2.9 s) and re-settle index first (5.6 s); the far fingers breathe (0.9 s), gather (3.05 s), the index lifts and settles (4.9 s), the hand strokes across the top (6.55 s); alive gate on
preflight.13: all of it small: thumb sweeps ≤ 10°, the lift ~2 px, the stroke ~4 px (gentle, warm brief)
